name: Necropolis of Bet She’arim: A Landmark of Jewish Renewal
description: Carved into soft limestone hills about 20 km east of Haifa, Bet She'arim is a vast underground cemetery of more than 30 catacomb systems. It became the main Jewish burial ground after the failed revolt against Rome, and Rabbi Judah the Patriarch was laid to rest here. Visitors can see ornate stone sarcophagi and walls covered in carvings and inscriptions in four languages.
